selfRoute.title: TierPlan's own route

detail.pending: The proxies are still picking up the route.
detail.waitingCertificate: Nothing is served on {{host}} until it is ready. {{direct}} keeps working.
detail.notAttachedSwarm: TierPlan's own service isn't on the tierplan-self network yet. Nothing is served on {{host}} until it is. Add the lines below to your stack file and deploy it again.
detail.notAttachedStandalone: TierPlan's container isn't on the tierplan-self network yet. TierPlan connects it itself on the next check.
detail.unknown: TierPlan couldn't read this just now.

selfRoute.offBody: Serve TierPlan itself on a hostname through ingress, with a certificate. It uses its own network, so the other routes can't reach TierPlan.

facts.directHelp: Keeps working. You can always reach TierPlan here, and turn the route off from here.

snippet.stack_file: TierPlan can't change its own service: an update would stop the task that sent it. Add these lines to your TierPlan stack file and deploy it again.
snippet.service_update: TierPlan's service wasn't deployed from a stack file, so add the network with this command on a manager.

refusal.self_route_needs_service: TierPlan runs as a plain container on a swarm node, and the route needs it to run as a swarm service. See <mono>install-in-swarm.md</mono>.
refusal.self_route_not_here: TierPlan can't tell whether it runs in this environment, so it won't switch its route on here. Direct access on <mono>{{direct}}</mono> isn't affected.

selfRoute.foreignMembers: Something other than the ingress proxy and TierPlan is on the tierplan-self network: <mono>{{members}}</mono>. TierPlan believes no client address forwarded over it until that leaves the network. Take it off tierplan-self.
selfRoute.usingRoute: You're using TierPlan through this route. If you turn it off, this page may stop answering. Open <mono>{{direct}}</mono> to carry on.
selfRoute.signIn: You sign in on each address separately. Single sign-on still returns to the public URL.
selfRoute.helper: Turning this on changes which origins and proxy addresses TierPlan trusts, so it needs an instance admin.
selfRoute.needsIngress: Turn ingress on first. The route is served by the proxies.

form.hostnameHelper: A name under a domain registered on the <domains>Domains tab</domains>. It can't be the host of the agent URL, or of the public URL when no agent URL is set.

selfRoute.offUsingRoute: You're using TierPlan through this route. This page may stop answering as the route goes. The change still goes through. Open {{direct}} to see the result.

vip.title: Virtual IP
vip.offBody: A virtual IP is one address that always points at a working proxy. It moves to another node if the one holding it fails.
vip.needsIngress: Turn ingress on first. The virtual IP points at the proxies.
vip.seeNodes: See who holds it on the Nodes tab.

form.addressHelper: The address with its prefix length. It must be unused and inside the network of every node.
form.routerIdHelper: Leave empty and TierPlan chooses one. Change it if another router on the network uses the same ID.

accessLog.title: Proxy access log
accessLog.helper: Records each request, including the client's address and the path asked for. Read it in the proxy's logs.

joinToken.none: No token has been made yet

rotate.title: Rotate the join token?
rotate.body: Nodes that are enrolled keep working. A node that enrols later needs the new token. The old one stops working at once.

disable.title: Disable the join token?
disable.body: No further node can enrol until you make a new one. Enrolled nodes keep working.

make.title: Make a new join token?
make.body: A node that enrols later needs this token. Enrolled nodes keep working.

redeploy.title: Stacks to redeploy
redeploy.note: Redeploy them after this finishes so they join the ingress network.

enable.title: Turn on ingress?
enable.body: TierPlan makes a join token, the ingress network and a proxy on each node. Stacks and their labels are not changed.
enable.failedHint: Nothing is lost. Turn it on again to carry on, or off to remove what was made.

disable.title: Turn off ingress?
disable.body: Routes stop being served on this environment. Stacks and their labels are not changed.
disable.failedHint: Nothing is lost. Turn it off again to remove what is left, or on to carry on.

vip.warningTitle: Read this before you turn it on
vip.warningText: The virtual IP needs `TIERPLAN_AGENT_ALLOW_PRIVILEGED_SERVICES=true` on every manager's agent. That setting lets TierPlan run privileged, host-network services on every node of this swarm, so a compromised TierPlan could take over every node. VRRP authentication only keeps honest neighbours apart; anything on this network segment can still contend for the address.

vipEnable.title: Turn on virtual IP?
vipEnable.body: Give the address the nodes will answer on. TierPlan checks it before anything is made.
vipEnable.failedHint: Nothing is lost. Turn it on again to carry on, or off to remove what was made.

vipChange.title: Change virtual IP?
vipChange.body: Change the address, the router ID or both. TierPlan checks them and says how the change is made before anything is touched.
vipChange.failedHint: Nothing is lost. Change it again to carry on, or turn the virtual IP off to remove what was made.

vipDisable.title: Turn off virtual IP?
vipDisable.body: Nodes stop answering on {{address}}. Ingress keeps serving on each node's own address.
vipDisable.failedHint: Nothing is lost. Turn it off again to remove what is left.

review.blockedBody: Fix the item marked Refused. Nothing has been changed.

snippet.title: Add TierPlan to the self network
snippet.stackFileNote: If the service has no `networks` entry yet, list the networks it already uses as well. A service with a `networks` entry leaves the default network.
snippet.note: TierPlan makes the tierplan-self network when you turn the route on. Run this after that. Direct access on {{direct}} isn't affected either way.

selfEnable.title: Turn on TierPlan's own route?
selfEnable.body: TierPlan makes the tierplan-self network and serves this app on the hostname you give, with a certificate. Direct access on {{direct}} keeps working, and you can turn the route off from there.
selfEnable.doneNotAttached: Add the lines on the card to your stack file to start serving.
selfEnable.failedHint: Nothing is lost. Turn it on again to carry on, or off to remove what was made. Direct access on {{direct}} still works.

selfDisable.title: Turn off TierPlan's own route?
selfDisable.body: TierPlan stops serving {{host}}. Direct access on {{direct}} keeps working. The hostname, its certificate and the tierplan-self network are kept only while something else needs them.
selfDisable.failedHint: Nothing is lost. Turn it off again to remove what is left. Direct access on {{direct}} still works.
